correctness.rationale: Necessity: for invertible T with TB⊂B and Tx=y, preimage of the exposed target minimal face intersects B in a face containing F(x); injectivity preserves affine dimension, so d(x)≤d(y). For sufficiency, let supporting norm-one functionals f,g expose F(x),F(y), k≤l. Choose isomorphism U:ker f→ker g sending L_x=span(F(x)−x) into L_y=span(F(y)−y). Tεz=f(z)y+εU(z−f(z)x) fixes x→y and is injective since g(Tεz)=f(z), U invertible on ker f. Each source vertex with f=1 maps into F(y) for small ε because y relative interior and U(v−x)∈L_y; f=−1 by central symmetry; |f|<1 maps into interior by ε→0. Finite vertices give common ε, hence contraction and invertibility. This works for nonsimple faces, n=1; relative openness/density of {d≥k} follows finite face lattice. n≥2 not semitransitive.
